shouldFix.title: The newly synchronised records disagree: a BLOCKER raised against v10 is recorded REPAIRED in the extended register but has no entry in the array the GOVERNING key rule says must list it
evidence: The key rule is GOVERNING and unambiguous. honestyRepairsKeyRule reads: 'GOVERNING. honestyRepairsFromVN lists findings raised against version N, repaired in a successor. It is not the generation that performed the repair. Refiling is not withdrawal. predecessorVerdictFindings is maintained from v6 onward with path, digest, verdict, and per-finding dispositions.'

The extended register records four Claude findings against v10, each REPAIRED: IR-HEA10-B1 at 'AR consentCarrier discriminator', IR-HEA10-B2 at 'requiredWhen registered', IR-HEA10-S1 at 'whenPresent object', IR-HEA10-S2 at 'remeasurementClause COORD scoping'.

honestyRepairsFromV10 carries only four entries and IR-HEA10-B2 is not among them: HAE10-CX-01, IR-HEA10-B1, IR-HEA10-S1, IR-HEA10-S2. A cross-check of every finding id in the register from v8 onward against every id in the honestyRepairsFrom* chain returns exactly one id present in the register and absent from the repair chain, and it is IR-HEA10-B2. The reverse direction is clean: zero repair entries lack a register finding.

The missing id is BLOCKER severity, not an advisory. The v10 Claude verdict, which this subject pins in recordedInputs at 92626bba and which reproduces, records IR-HEA10-B2 with severity BLOCKER and the title 'v10 mints a new predicate that the narrowed rule no longer reaches and the new domain does not enumerate, leaving it governed by nothing'.

The gap is in the specific structure v14 introduced to close this class of gap. CLAUDE-HEA13-S1 asked for one stated reading with entries refiled to it, and Codex HAE13-CX-02 asked for the register extension; v14 delivered both and then shipped a disagreement between them.

The substantive repair does appear to exist, which bounds the severity. honestyRepairsFromV10[0] records HAE10-CX-01 as 'Both carrier predicates registered', which is the same subject matter as the register's 'at' string for IR-HEA10-B2, and consentCarrierPredicateDomain.appliesTo does now enumerate all four predicate targets. What is missing is the accounting entry, not the fix. But the GOVERNING rule admits no joint-coverage shorthand: it says honestyRepairsFromVN lists findings raised against version N, without exception for findings repaired alongside another.
shouldFix.impact: A reviewer applying the artifact's own GOVERNING rule to answer 'were all findings raised against v10 addressed?' reads honestyRepairsFromV10, finds four entries, and does not find IR-HEA10-B2. Only a reader who additionally cross-references the register notices that a fifth finding exists and is claimed repaired. That is the same accounting failure CLAUDE-HEA13-S1 and HAE13-CX-02 were raised to close, surviving in the machinery built to close it, and it attaches to a BLOCKER rather than a minor finding. Because the two structures now assert different v10 finding sets, neither can be relied on alone, which is precisely the property the repair was meant to establish.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add an IR-HEA10-B2 entry to honestyRepairsFromV10 describing its repair, in the same form as its three siblings. If it was genuinely discharged by the HAE10-CX-01 repair rather than separately, say so in that entry and add a joint-coverage clause to honestyRepairsKeyRule so the rule permits what the record does. Then re-run the cross-check in both directions, register to repair chain and back, so the two structures assert the same finding set for every round from v8 onward.

advisories.title: The extended register rounds omit advisory-severity findings that the rounds they extend record
advisories.observation: The historical rounds carry advisories in the same findings arrays as blockers and should-fixes: the v1 entry lists IR-HEA1-A1/A2/A3 beside IR-HEA1-B1, and the v5 entry lists IR-HEA5-A1 alone. The new rounds do not. Against my three frozen verdicts, which the register pins at digests that reproduce, v9 carried CLAUDE-HEA9-A1/A2/A3, v11 carried A1/A2 and v13 carried A1/A2; the register records only the single should-fix id for each of those rounds.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: Advisories are by construction non-blocking and several of mine were explicitly recorded as not adopted, so omitting them cannot conceal an unaddressed gating finding, which is what the register exists to prevent. The blocking findings for every round from v8 onward are recorded completely, and I verified all twelve round entries carry an accurate path, digest and verdict. This is a shape inconsistency against the earlier rounds rather than a loss of gating information.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional. Either carry advisories in the new rounds as the old ones do, or state in honestyRepairsKeyRule that the register records blocking findings only from v8 onward.

I checked all twelve new round entries rather than sampling: each carries a path, a sha256 and a verdict, and the non-ACCEPT rounds carry per-finding ids with dispositions. I then verified every one against the working tree: twelve of twelve digests reproduce and twelve of twelve recorded verdict words match the actual verdict field in the pinned file, including my own v9, v11 and v13 verdicts and the v8 dual ACCEPT that underlies D-093. That is a materially stronger record than the artifact had at any earlier generation.
measurements.hae13Cx01Detail: Judged against Codex's frozen BLOCKER text, which offered two options and preferred requiring the member present. v14 takes that option and carries it through every place the representation is described: consentCarrierPredicateDomain.rule now reads 'policyProvenance MUST be a present JSON member'; a new omission clause reads 'refuse — omitted policyProvenance is not a legal encoding of invocation-time-naming'; roundTrip is restated over 'present JSON null' and 'present source-identity object' with 'Omitted member refuses'; destinations.consentCarrier states 'Omitted policyProvenance has no inverse and refuses'; destinations.policyProvenance now requires presence at both the record and the scope projection and no longer contains the word absent that previously licensed omission. FC-CARRIER-SHAPE gains four rows: an omitted record member refusing, a missing-digest object refusing, a NOT-HEX digest with an extra key refusing, and an omitted scope projection refusing. Codex's closing requirement, that every legal emitted representation have a declared inverse, holds: two legal representations, two inverses, omission explicitly outside the domain.
measurements.presenceAtBothLayersDetail: I tested whether the serialized layer actually carries the presence obligation or only the record layer does, since a one-sided repair is this lineage's recurring failure and I have raised it twice. The record member carries required true; the serialized member carries no required key. That is not an asymmetry: no member of the fifteen-member serialized shape carries a required key, because membership in the closed list is what establishes presence there and nullable governs null versus value. The serialized presence obligation is carried normatively in three independent places, destinations.policyProvenance, consentCarrierPredicateDomain.rule and its omission clause, and FC-CARRIER-SHAPE's omitted-projection row. This candidate finding is refuted.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. Both claimed repairs are real and this is the best-evidenced generation of this lineage: Codex's HAE13-CX-01 blocker is repaired on its preferred option and carried through every description of the representation, with omission given no inverse and four new refusal rows; the register is extended a round further than asked and every one of its twelve entries verifies against the working tree for digest and verdict; and my own finding's two clauses are both met, with eighteen of eighteen repair entries now consistent with a GOVERNING key rule that did not exist a generation ago. I also refuted a candidate finding of my own after checking the serialized shape's conventions. What remains is narrow and provable only because v14 built the machinery that exposes it: the register asserts that IR-HEA10-B2, a BLOCKER raised against v10, was REPAIRED, while honestyRepairsFromV10 omits it, so the two structures the repair synchronised disagree about the v10 finding set. Since the whole purpose of both v13 findings was that either structure alone should be trustworthy, that does not clear the bar. One entry closes it.
